pmc-12495465.title: Prospective evaluation of an AI-enabled elastic scattering spectroscopy device for triage of patient-identified skin lesions in dermatology clinics

pmc-12495465.description: ncer presentations are often first noticed by patients.2,3 A highly sensitive Elastic Scattering Spectroscopy (ESS) device integrated with artificial intelligence (AI) utilizing spectral scans was cleared for adjunct usage in primary care and is the only FDA-cleared tool for evaluating all 3 common types of skin cancer (melanoma, basal cell carcinoma [BCC], and squamous cell carcinoma [SCC]).

pmc-12535019.title: Effectiveness of a multidisciplinary team teaching method on breastfeeding knowledge of nursing students in China: a randomized controlled trial
pmc-12535019.creator: Qingkun Han, Tingting Gao, Cuiping Li, Xuebing Jing
pmc-12535019.description: BackgroundSpecial breastfeeding training is rare in China and contradicts clinical expectations for students.Multidisciplinary team (MDT) approaches have been extensively advocated in nursing education. However, the incorporation of MDT education to enhance students' knowledge of breastfeeding remains insufficient and constrained.ObjectiveTo examine the change in knowledge of nursing students in China following a clinical MDT education intervention on breastfeeding.

pmc-12737020.title: Biomonitoring of Silver in Children and Adolescents from Alcalá de Henares (Spain): Assessing Potential Health Risks from Topsoil Contamination
pmc-12737020.creator: Antonio Peña-Fernández, Manuel Higueras, Roberto Valiente, M. Carmen Lobo-Bedmar
pmc-12737020.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This study assessed exposure to silver (Ag) in children and adolescents living in Alcalá de Henares, an urban-industrial city in the Madrid Region (Spain), in light of the growing use of Ag in consumer and medical products. Scalp hair was collected from 120 children (6–9 years; 70 females) and 97 adolescents (13–16 years; 68 females) permanently residing in the city, and Ag concentrations were determined by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry under strict quality control.

pmc-12793857.title: Sleep Health and Associations With Early Cardiovascular Risk in U.S. Collegiate Female Athletes
pmc-12793857.creator: Austin J. Rim, J.T. Miller, Mekensie Jackson, Yi-An Ko, Neeya Patel, Sanchitha Rajesh, Heather DiGregorio, Rayan El Chami, Jennifer Mansour, Muhammad Owais, James Sherrer, Erin Simpson, Braxton Walker, Sophia Wolmer, Angelo Galante, Craig Clark, Aaron L. Baggish, Donald L. Bliwise, Jonathan H. Kim
pmc-12793857.description: BackgroundSleep apnea is common among male competitive athletes and may be associated with early cardiovascular risk. Among female athletes, the prevalence and outcomes of sleep apnea have not been described.ObjectivesThe objective of the study was to comprehensively assess sleep health and associations with markers of cardiovascular risk in an observational cohort of U.S. collegiate female athletes.

pmc-13234737.title: Comprehensive longitudinal profiling identifies differential frequency, epitope specificity, and effector function of CD8+ T-cells across COVID-19 disease severities
pmc-13234737.creator: Susana Patricia Amaya Hernandez, Kamilla Kjærgaard Munk, Konstantin Danilov, Mohammad Kadivar, Ditte Stampe Hersby, Tripti Tamhane, Simone Majken Stegenborg-Grathwohl, Anders Gorm Pedersen, Anne Ortved Gang, Sine Reker Hadrup, Sunil Kumar Saini
pmc-13234737.description: SummaryBackgroundCD8+ T-cells are crucial for controlling and resolving SARS-CoV-2 infection, yet their epitope specificity and relationship to COVID-19 disease severity remain incompletely understood.MethodsWe performed comprehensive longitudinal profiling of antigen-specific CD8+ T-cell populations using DNA-barcoded peptide–HLA multimers, analysing 553 SARS-CoV-2 epitopes across globally prevalent HLA alleles in patients with mild and severe COVID-19.

pmc-13246596.title: Primary care visit trends in a public safety net health system during the COVID-19 pandemic
pmc-13246596.creator: Cristina Valdovinos, Yu-Chuang Huang, Stefanie Vassar, Griselda Gutierrez, Carmen Mendez, Anshu Abhat, Arleen Brown, Alejandra Casillas
pmc-13246596.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundLittle is known about access to care and telehealth trends in safety net settings during the Coronavirus-19 (COVID-19) pandemic.MethodsWe analyzed electronic health record data from patients assigned to a large, publicly funded, urban safety net system for primary care.

pmc-13272605.title: Healthcare contact days in cancer survivors relative to those with no cancer history
pmc-13272605.creator: Helen M. Parsons, Christina C. Newton, Arjun Gupta, W. Dana Flanders, Alpa V. Patel, Clara Bodelon, Charlie Zhong, J. Lee Westmaas, Erika Rees-Punia
pmc-13272605.description: IntroductionCancer survivors have unique healthcare needs that require frequent contact with the healthcare system to receive cancer-directed treatment and survivorship care. While there is growing evidence of survivors’ time burden for cancer care, we have less information about the trajectory of this burden across a broad range of cancers relative to those without cancer.

pmc-13332549.title: Quantitative MRI Assessment of Myotoxin‐Induced Skeletal Muscle Damage of mdx Mice
pmc-13332549.creator: Ravneet Vohra, Joshua Park, Feng Zhang, Jeffrey S. Chamberlain, Donghoon Lee
pmc-13332549.description: Introduction/AimsAlthough magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has been extensively applied in dystrophic muscle, longitudinal characterization of multiple quantitative MRI parameters during degeneration and regeneration remains limited. This study aimed to longitudinally characterize changes in quantitative MRI parameters in control and dystrophic mouse muscles following myotoxin‐induced myonecrosis using multi‐parametric MRI (mpMRI).

pmc-13552167.title: Surgical Procedure for Osteophyte Impingement of the Quadriceps Tendon: A Case Report
pmc-13552167.creator: Hiroya Akase, Masashi Hirakawa, Nobuhiro Kaku
pmc-13552167.description: Introduction:Osteophytes associated with knee osteoarthritis can irritate surrounding soft tissues and cause pain and mechanical symptoms. Although impingement of the medial collateral ligament and popliteus tendon has been reported, symptomatic osteophyte impingement of the quadriceps tendon is rare, and no reports describe its surgical treatment.

pmc-13573539.title: Dose-Registered CT assessment of radiation-induced lung injury after chemoradiotherapy for stage III NSCLC
pmc-13573539.creator: Tomohiro Itonaga, Ryuji Mikami, Tatsuhiko Zama, Mitsuru Okubo, Shinji Sugahara, Norihiko Ikeda, Kazuhiro Saito
pmc-13573539.description: AimsTo quantify radiation-induced lung injury (RILI) on deformably registered CT images after chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) for stage III NSCLC, and to evaluate spatial and dosimetric associations between RILI and planned dose distribution in a pre-durvalumab cohort.MethodsThis retrospective study included 58 patients with stage III NSCLC treated with CCRT using three-dimensional conformal radiotherapy (3D-CRT) prior to the era of consolidation immunotherapy.

uslaw-usc-t18-s117.title: 18 U.S.C. § 117 — Domestic assault by an habitual offender
uslaw-usc-t18-s117.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t18-s117.description: United States Code, Title 18 (Crimes And Criminal Procedure); Part I (Crimes); Chapter 7 (Assault). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) In General.— Any person who commits a domestic assault within the special maritime and territorial jurisdiction of the United States or Indian country and who has a final conviction on at least 2 separate prior occasions in Federal, State, or Indian.
